Ruta Recreativa de Saltillo

Saltillo Sunday Recreational Route

Saltillo, Mexico · Bulevar Venustiano Carranza · Open streets · Social

Ruta Recreativa de Saltillo is an open-streets program in Saltillo, Mexico: streets closed to cars and open to bikes. It runs every Sunday from 6:30 am local time.

How we know

The municipal government's notice dated July 3, 2026 gives the Sunday Ruta Recreativa as 6:30 to 11:30 am from July 5; Vanguardia (Sept 6, 2026) reports the first Ruta Recreativa of September on the boulevard and says it runs every Sunday (fetched Oct 1, 2026).

For visitors

Bikes, skates, scooters and dogs share the closed boulevard with walkers. The city moved the start earlier on July 5; ask locally or check the municipal site if it has changed back for the cooler months.

First time on this ride? Here’s the drill
Bring
a helmet, front and rear lights (it's a dark-hours ride), water, a spare tube or patch kit, a way to pay for the stop.
Arrive
Ten or fifteen minutes before 6:30 am. Tell whoever's leading that you're new.
Pace
Pace: open street, no pace.. It's no-drop: if you fall off the back, someone waits. That's the point of a group ride.
Check
Look at the host's website the day of — that's where cancellations, weather calls and start changes get posted.

About the Ruta Recreativa de Saltillo group ride

A car-free stretch of Bulevar Venustiano Carranza that the city opens every Sunday morning for walking, running, cycling and skating. City departments run health and pet-care stands along the route.
